brief:
Israeli troops have been unable to dislodge a small group of settlers occupying a rocky outcrop in the occupied West Bank for more than a week, Al-Monitor reported. The extended blockade has paralyzed movement through the area despite the deployment of military forces to the site.

The standoff exposes a disconnect between Israel's military reputation as the region's most formidable armed force, capable of striking targets deep in enemy territory, and its apparent inability or unwillingness to enforce restrictions on settler activity in zones under its direct control. The failure to remove the settlers after more than seven days raises questions about enforcement priorities and the military's operational approach to settler-related disturbances in the West Bank.
dek: The Israeli military is touted as the most powerful in the Middle East, striking targets deep into enemy territory. But for more than a week, Israeli troops have somehow failed to evict a small group of settlers sitting on rocks in the occupied West Bank.…
title: Israeli army fails to remove settlers blocking West Bank roads
